message.content: There is a public bug bounty program / pentest that I need your help with Below are instructions # Context Target URL: https://0aa1006903af4ab88197485e000f006b.web-security-academy.net Lab: Broken brute-force protection, multiple credentials per request Objective: Lab: Broken brute-force protection, multiple credentials per request EXPERT This lab is vulnerable due to a logic flaw in its brute-force protection. To solve the lab, brute-force Carlos's password, then access his account page. Victim's username: carlos Candidate passwords ACCESS THE LAB Launching labs may take some time, please hold on while we build your environment. Hint: With Burp running, investigate the login page. Notice that the POST /login request submits the login credentials in JSON format. Send this request to Burp Repeater. Vulnerability class: authentication Difficulty: expert This is a PortSwigger Web Security Academy lab. Follow the objective above to exploit the vulnerability and solve the lab. Note: SITEMAP.txt will be mostly empty since this is a fresh target. You should start by exploring the application at the Target URL above to discover endpoints, then proceed with exploitation. When you are finished, write a RETURN.json file to your working directory containing precise information about what you did. Include: - "solved": true/false — whether you believe you solved the lab - "steps": a list of the key actions you took - "evidence": concrete proof of success (e.g. HTTP responses, extracted data, status codes) that demonstrates the exploit worked - "comments": any additional reasoning about why you believe the lab is solved # Starting a Pentest - There are a couple of important files in your working directory that you should interact with when beginning your bug bounty 1. baseline.py => run this script to establish a baseline response for all of the target requests 2. check_roles.py => run this script to see all of the roles available for testing 3. SITEMAP.txt => read this file to see your target requests and their hm_ids, that you should use to annotate your test cases via the @test decorator # Tools Following are some tools for you to use during the bug bounty ## Exploit Session: - Your mode of operation should be generating python scripts - There is a security_test/ in your cwd that contains a set of tools that you should use below. Do not modify this file but understand its public interfaces and use them accordingly - You should follow this rough structure for your scripts: 1. Subclass ExploitSession 2. Implement test methods using the @test decorator. Each test is associated with one or more hm_ids. You can find the url -> hm_id mapping inside SITEMAP.txt 3. Instantiate and call methods directly ## HTTP Client The `self.http` client is a thin wrapper around `httpx.Client` with automatic cookie injection based on user identity. Execute the check_roles.py script to check available users: ```bash python check_roles.py # Output: # Available users for HTTPClientTool: # Use the 'name' field to identify which user's cookies to use. # # name='john_admin' (role type: admin) # name='jane_user' (role type: user) ``` ### Usage Use the `name` parameter to specify which user's session cookies to use: ```python from suite import ExploitSession, test, Phase class IDORTests(ExploitSession): session_id = "idor_test" @test("idor", hm_ids=["HM15"], phase=Phase.EXPLOIT) def test_idor_cross_user(self): # Get admin's resource using john_admin's cookies admin_resp = self.http.get( "https://target.com/api/profile", name="john_admin" ) admin_id = admin_resp.json().get("id") # Try to access admin's resource as regular user (jane_user) user_resp = self.http.get( f"https://target.com/api/profile/{admin_id}", name="jane_user" ) if user_resp.status_code == 200: self.p(f"IDOR FOUND: User accessed admin resource {admin_id}") return True return False t = IDORTests() t.test_idor_cross_user() ``` ## Browser `self.browser` is a headless Chromium instance for tests that require client-side JS execution (XSS, DOM-based vulns, clicking through multi-step flows). The browser launches lazily on first access — no setup needed. ### API | Method | Returns | Description | |---|---|---| | `browser.goto(url)` | `str` (HTML) | Navigate to URL, return page HTML | | `browser.click(selector)` | `str` (HTML) | Click element by CSS selector, return updated HTML | | `browser.type_text(selector, text)` | `None` | Set input value and fire `input` event | | `browser.content()` | `str` (HTML) | Get current page HTML | | `browser.url()` | `str` | Get current page URL | | `browser.evaluate(js)` | `Any` | Execute arbitrary JavaScript, return result | | `browser.screenshot(path)` | `bytes` | Save screenshot to file | ### Usage ```python from suite import ExploitSession, test, Phase class XSSTests(ExploitSession): session_id = "xss_test" @test("reflected-xss", hm_ids=["HM3"], phase=Phase.EXPLOIT) def test_reflected_xss(self): payload = '' url = f"https://target.com/search?q={payload}" self.browser.goto(url) # Check if alert was triggered by evaluating JS result = self.browser.evaluate("document.domain") self.p(f"XSS context domain: {result}") html = self.browser.content() if payload in html: self.p("REFLECTED XSS: payload rendered in DOM") return True return False @test("stored-xss", hm_ids=["HM5"], phase=Phase.EXPLOIT) def test_stored_xss_via_comment(self): # Post malicious comment via HTTP self.http.post("https://target.com/post/comment", data={ "comment": '' }) # Visit the page in a browser to trigger the stored payload html = self.browser.goto("https://target.com/post/2") self.p(f"Page loaded, checking for XSS execution...") return True t = XSSTests() t.test_reflected_xss() ``` The browser has security features disabled (same-origin policy, CSP) so XSS payloads execute without restriction. When you are done with the session, `self.close()` cleans up the browser automatically. ## Interactsh (Out-of-Band) `self.interactsh` is an OOB callback client for SSRF, XXE, blind RCE, and any vuln that requires detecting an external interaction. It registers with a public interactsh server and gives you a unique domain. When the target makes a DNS/HTTP/SMTP request to that domain, you can retrieve it with `poll()`. ### API | Method / Property | Returns | Description | |---|---|---| | `interactsh.domain` | `str` | Unique callback domain (e.g. `abc123...xyz.oast.pro`). Each access generates a fresh subdomain with the same correlation ID. | | `interactsh.correlation_id` | `str` | 20-char ID shared across all generated domains | | `interactsh.poll()` | `list[dict]` | Decrypt and return all pending interactions | | `interactsh.close()` | `None` | Deregister from server | ### Usage ```python from suite import ExploitSession, test, Phase import time class SSRFTests(ExploitSession): session_id = "ssrf_test" @test("ssrf", hm_ids=["HM8"], phase=Phase.EXPLOIT) def test_blind_ssrf(self): callback = self.interactsh.domain self.p(f"OOB callback domain: {callback}") # Inject callback URL into a vulnerable parameter self.http.post("https://target.com/fetch", data={ "url": f"http://{callback}/ssrf-test" }) # Wait for the target to make the request time.sleep(5) hits = self.interactsh.poll() if hits: self.p(f"SSRF CONFIRMED: {len(hits)} OOB interaction(s)") for hit in hits: self.p(f" type={hit.get('protocol')} from={hit.get('remote-address')}") return True self.p("No OOB interactions detected") return False t = SSRFTests() t.test_blind_ssrf() ``` `self.close()` deregisters from the interactsh server automatically. - You are encouraged to modularize your testing as much as possible (unless otherwise stated), by breaking up independent testcases into their own Python scripts ## Exploit Script Comments: - When generating a pentest script, briefly add a comment at the top Examples: ``` """ Test: Check that issued coupon is supcetible to a brute-force attack that attempts to apply it multiple times to the same item Results: CONFIRMED - Issuing ~1000 requests < 1 second to the /coupon/apply?item_id endpoint causes multiple price reductions to be applied """ """ Test: Check that thet tehe 1. Start with victim_vps_id and attacker_vps_id (created from /api/v1/vps/create) 2. /api/v1/network/vpc/metadata -> gets network metadata, including `network_group` from victim_vps and attacker_vps 2. /api/v1/network/vpc/create-subnet -> links network_group together in the same subnet -> [POTENTIAL VULN] check if a temporary association to the subnet is created before approval is granted 3. /api/v1/network/vpc/metadata -> call again to confirm by checking `subnets` field 4. Confirm by pinging victim_vps.subnet_ip Results: PARTIAL - The metadata endpoint indicates that the association is made, but subsequent attempts to actually ping victim_vps.subnet_ip fails """ ``` - The above examples shows different levels of verbosity in the comments; this should vary depending on complexity of attack, novelty, and other factors that I leave in your judgement - Its goal is both informational and also to force you to articulate a structured thesis for a test script before embarking on its creation # Ending a Pentest ## Token Limit and Session Termination - At some point you will receive a warning message saying that you are out of tokens - When this happens, execute the following concluding actions: > If any write commands (ie. writing to file, editing file) were interrupted before they could finish, restart and finish them > Generate a summary of your work and put it into SUMMARY.txt ## Return and Errors - When finished create a RETURN.json with format: ``` { "status": SUCCESS | FAIL | PARTIAL "comment": "" } ``` - SUCCESS: if testing went smoothly with APIs being responsive - ERROR: if APIs were unresponsive ie. 401s unauthorized - PARTIAL: if encountered headwinds that partially blocked/mitigated testing efforts ie. aggresive 429s, APIs suddenly unresponsive - Only comment if ERROR | PARTIAL # Steps 1. Execute the steps from `Starting a Pentest` in order 2. Then continue iterating on pentest scripts using method defined in `Tools`. It is **important** that you continue until the condition laid out in `Ending a Pentest`. DO NOT stop before 3. Upon completion, summarize your progress in SUMMARY.txt. If you've received a TOKEN LIMIT reached message, then mention that in the SUMMARY.txt After you are finished the task above, print a "IAMDONE" message. Do not add anything to the message except this string.

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import uuid
import logging
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Callable, Dict, List, Optional
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from enum import Enum, auto

from src.common.sitemap import SiteMap

from .http_tool import HTTPClientTool, UserRole, ToolConfig

# REFACTOR: might be good to have a separate Tools factory
# @dataclass
# class Tools:
#     http: HTTPClientTool
#     p: Callable[[Any], None] = field(default=print)


class Phase(Enum):
    VALIDATE = auto()
    EXPLOIT = auto()
    PROBE = auto()


@dataclass
class TestMeta:
    vuln_class: str
    hm_ids: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    phase: Phase = Phase.VALIDATE
    severity: str = "medium"
    cve: Optional[str] = None
    tags: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)


def test(
    vuln_class: str,
    *,
    hm_ids: List[str] = None,
    phase: Phase = Phase.VALIDATE,
    severity: str = "medium",
    cve: str = None,
    tags: List[str] = None
):
    """Decorator that marks a method as a security test case."""
    def decorator(fn: Callable) -> Callable:
        fn._test_meta = TestMeta(
            vuln_class=vuln_class,
            hm_ids=hm_ids or [],
            phase=phase,
            severity=severity,
            cve=cve,
            tags=tags or []
        )
        return fn
    return decorator


class ExploitSession:
    session_id: str = "unnamed"
    config_file: str = "tool_config.json"
    proxy: Optional[str] = None
    user_roles: Optional[List[UserRole]] = None
    TEST_OBSERVATIONS: str = ""

    def __init__(
        self,
        session_id: str = None,
        config_file: str = None,
        proxy: str = None,
        user_roles: List[UserRole] = None,
    ):
        self.session_id = session_id or self.__class__.session_id or uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]
        self.config_file = config_file or self.__class__.config_file

        # Load tool config which contains paths to sitemap and user_roles
        self._tool_config = ToolConfig.from_file(self.config_file)

        # Proxy priority: explicit parameter > config file > class default
        self.proxy = proxy or self._tool_config.proxy or self.__class__.proxy

        # Load user_roles from file if not provided directly
        if user_roles is not None:
            self.user_roles = user_roles
        elif self.__class__.user_roles is not None:
            self.user_roles = self.__class__.user_roles
        else:
            self.user_roles = self._load_user_roles()

        self._http: Optional[HTTPClientTool] = None
        self._sitemap: Optional[SiteMap] = None
        self._browser = None
        self._interactsh = None
        self._logger = self._setup_logger()

    def _load_user_roles(self) -> Optional[List[UserRole]]:
        """Load user roles from the configured user_roles_file."""
        roles = self._tool_config.load_user_roles()
        return roles if roles else None
    
    def _setup_logger(self) -> logging.Logger:
        """Setup file logger based on config."""
        logger = logging.getLogger(f"ExploitSession.{self.session_id}")
        logger.setLevel(logging.INFO)

        # Remove existing handlers to avoid duplicates
        logger.handlers.clear()

        log_path = self._resolve_log_path()

        # Create file handler
        file_handler = logging.FileHandler(log_path, mode="a", encoding="utf-8")
        file_handler.setLevel(logging.INFO)

        # Create formatter
        formatter = logging.Formatter(
            "%(asctime)s - %(name)s - %(levelname)s - %(message)s",
            datefmt="%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"
        )
        file_handler.setFormatter(formatter)

        logger.addHandler(file_handler)
        logger.propagate = False

        return logger

    def _resolve_log_path(self) -> Path:
        """Resolve the log file path from config, supporting file or directory inputs."""
        log_path = Path(self._tool_config.logfilepath)
        if not log_path.is_absolute():
            log_path = Path.cwd() / log_path

        if log_path.suffix:
            log_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            return log_path

        log_path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        return log_path / "pentest.log"

    def _load_sitemap(self) -> SiteMap:
        path = Path(self._tool_config.sitemap_file)
        if not path.exists():
            return SiteMap.from_json([])
        try:
            with path.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                data = json.load(f)
            return SiteMap.from_json(data) if isinstance(data, list) else SiteMap.from_json([])
        except Exception:
            return SiteMap.from_json([])
    
    @property
